endorsements.quote: This function might even help to distinguish between users showing signs of transient thinking bias due to recent frustration and those developing psychotic ideation, with appropriate follow-up support provi ded by the AI (e.g., self-help guidance for mild psychological problems but immediate referral to professional human support for cases of suicidal ideation, thereby supporting actual regulation of em otion (4)).

Even after comprehensive safety testing, it might also be desirable to embed deployed systems in stepped-care contexts with clinical supervision, while making explicit under what circumstances humans should assume full control.

unlisted_practices: Test emotionally aware AI systems first with stable healthy participants and then with patient groups under clear human supervision so observers can intervene immediately if overreliance or strengthened cognitive biases occur.
Fine-tune AI companions against amplifying cognitive biases, even at the cost of reducing emotional warmth in some contexts.
Design AI systems to respond flexibly to a user's emotional state depending on context, using real-time monitoring of multimodal emotional cues, rather than a one-size-fits-all communication style.
Align emotional AI systems with regulatory requirements for safety and risk management.
Tune LLMs to an appropriate level of agreeableness rather than eliminating agreeable communication.
Validate emotion regulation capabilities of AI systems using neuroscientific techniques and other data streams such as keystroke dynamics or facial expressions.
Combine AI companion design with mitigation strategies such as stimulating user reflection on outcomes or providing users metacognitive strategies to resist sycophantic AI.
